---
title: "Figure 7.1: Real GDP Growth (projections)"
---

![Python: `python/fig-7-1.py`](../images/python/fig-7-1.png)

Annual real GDP growth, with projections to 2028, for the United States,
Canada and three Latin American and Caribbean groups. The Caribbean is shown
twice:

- **excluding Guyana and Suriname**, as a solid line on the left scale;
- **including them**, as a dashed line on the right scale, because their
  very fast growth, driven by new oil production, would otherwise squeeze
  the scale for everyone else.

**New in this chart:** a dashed series, also dashed in the legend.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 7 rows (2022 to 2028):

| category | USA | CAN | LA7 | CAPDR | CARIB (excl. GUY/SUR) | CARIB (right scale) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 2.43 | 4.70 | 3.61 | 5.61 | 4.66 | 13.80 |

Six series, the years as numbers. The two Caribbean columns show how much
Guyana and Suriname matter: in 2022, 4.66 percent growth without them and
13.80 percent with them.

## The script

### The series

```python
left_series = {
    "USA": "#145A8D",
    "CAN": "#4D4D4D",
    "LA7": "#66338A",
    "CAPDR": "#C95A0A",
    "CARIB (excl. GUY/SUR)": "#00A1A9",
}
right_series = "CARIB (right scale)"
right_colour = "#00A1A9"
dashed = (0, (3, 2))
```

The five left-scale series go in a dictionary for the loop. The right-scale
series is kept apart, because it is drawn on a different axes object.

Both Caribbean series use the same teal: they are the same region, and the
dash is what tells them apart.

The dash pattern is stored in a name, `dashed`, because it is used twice:
for the line and for its legend entry. Writing it once guarantees that the
two match. `(0, (3, 2))` means: start at the beginning of the pattern, then
repeat a dash 3 line widths long and a gap 2 line widths long. See [Line
styles](../techniques.qmd#sec-line-styles).

### Two scales

```python
for series, colour in left_series.items():
    ax.plot(years, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round")

# CARIB including Guyana and Suriname grows much faster, so it is shown
# dashed on the right-hand scale.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (4, 16), 2)
ax_right.plot(years, data[right_series], color=right_colour, linewidth=1.8,
              linestyle=dashed)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
```

The loop draws the five left-scale lines on `ax`. Then `add_right_axis()`
creates `ax_right`, with its own y-axis on the right from 4 to 16, and the
dashed Caribbean line is drawn on it. See [A right-hand
scale](../chart-style.qmd#sec-right-axis).

The left scale runs from 0 to 6 in steps of 1 and the right from 4 to 16 in
steps of 2. Both have six intervals, so the ticks line up: 0 on the left is
level with 4 on the right, 1 with 6, and so on. See [A right-hand
scale](../techniques.qmd#sec-right-scale).

None of the lines has a `label=`, because the legend is built by hand.

### The axes

```python
ax.set_xlim(2021.5, 2028.5)
ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=2.8, pad=5)

set_y_scale(ax, 0, 6, 1)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
```

Seven years, all labelled, with half a year of margin at each end. The left
scale is set with the shared helper `set_y_scale()`.

### A legend with a dashed entry

```python
handles = [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=1.8) for c in left_series.values()]
handles.append(Line2D([], [], color=right_colour, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=dashed))
ax_right.legend(handles, [*left_series, right_series],
                loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.4, 1.0),
                handlelength=3.4, labelspacing=0.05)
```

The legend has one solid sample line per left-scale series and one dashed
line for the right-scale series.

- **The samples.** `Line2D([], [], ...)` is a line with no data, used only
  for the legend. The list comprehension makes five solid ones, one per
  colour, and `handles.append(...)` adds a sixth with
  `linestyle=dashed`. A legend sample copies whatever style it is given, so
  the dash shows up in the legend exactly as in the chart.
- **The names.** `[*left_series, right_series]` builds the list of names:
  `*` unpacks the dictionary's keys, followed by one more name. The result
  is `["USA", "CAN", "LA7", "CAPDR", "CARIB (excl. GUY/SUR)", "CARIB (right
  scale)"]`, in the same order as the handles.
- **Placement.** The legend is anchored by its top-left corner at 40
  percent across the plot, at the top, where the lines leave room. It goes
  on `ax_right`, the top layer, so no line covers it.
- **Visible dashes.** `handlelength=3.4` makes the sample lines long enough
  for the dashes to show; at the default length of 2, the sample would show
  only one or two dashes.
- `labelspacing=0.05` packs the six entries closely, so the legend fits in
  the space above the lines.

See [Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## Changing the chart

- **Projections shaded.** To mark the projection years, add
  `ax.axvspan(2025.5, 2028.5, color="#F2F2F2", zorder=0)` before drawing the
  lines.
- **All on one scale.** If a new edition no longer needs the right scale,
  draw the dashed line on `ax`, delete the `add_right_axis()` line and widen
  the left scale, for example `set_y_scale(ax, 0, 16, 2)`.
- **Another dash.** `(0, (1, 1))` gives a dotted line, `(0, (6, 2, 1, 2))` a
  dash-dot pattern.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-7-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-7-1.py"}
"""Figure 7.1: Real GDP Growth (projections)."""
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from chart_style import (
    add_right_axis,
    new_chart,
    read_chart_data,
    save_chart,
    set_y_scale,
)

STEM = "fig-7-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)
years = data["category"]

left_series = {
    "USA": "#145A8D",
    "CAN": "#4D4D4D",
    "LA7": "#66338A",
    "CAPDR": "#C95A0A",
    "CARIB (excl. GUY/SUR)": "#00A1A9",
}
right_series = "CARIB (right scale)"
right_colour = "#00A1A9"
dashed = (0, (3, 2))

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Real GDP Growth",
    subtitle="(Year-over-year percent change)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook database; and IMF staff\n"
        "calculations.\n"
        "Note: Aggregates are purchasing-power-parity GDP-weighted average.\n"
        "CAPDR = Central America, Panama, and the Dominican Republic; CARIB\n"
        "= Caribbean; LA7 = Latin America 7 (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico,\n"
        "Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay)."
    ),
    left=0.3,
    right=0.35,
    bottom_gap=0.3,
)

for series, colour in left_series.items():
    ax.plot(years, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round")

# CARIB including Guyana and Suriname grows much faster, so it is shown
# dashed on the right-hand scale.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (4, 16), 2)
ax_right.plot(years, data[right_series], color=right_colour, linewidth=1.8,
              linestyle=dashed)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)

ax.set_xlim(2021.5, 2028.5)
ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=2.8, pad=5)

set_y_scale(ax, 0, 6, 1)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)

handles = [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=1.8) for c in left_series.values()]
handles.append(Line2D([], [], color=right_colour, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=dashed))
ax_right.legend(handles, [*left_series, right_series],
                loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.4, 1.0),
                handlelength=3.4, labelspacing=0.05)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
